messages:
anya: quick note from today's stress run: allocator kept reassigning to shards that were freshly preempted. led to tenant throttle spikes.
anya: repro: `go test ./orchestrator -run TestFallbackLoop`
any log excerpt:
2026-03-18T10:00:01Z INFO admit shard=shard-5 tenant=tn-3 tokens=256
2026-03-18T10:00:01Z WARN preempt evict shard=shard-5 reason=preemptible-credit-exhausted
2026-03-18T10:00:01Z INFO fallback reroute req=foo -> shard-12
2026-03-18T10:00:01Z WARN preempt evict shard=shard-12 reason=hotspot
2026-03-18T10:00:02Z ERROR admission throttle spike tenant=tn-3 rate=420/s
deep: sounds like we need a flapping detector + cooldown. simple rules: count preempts in 60s + reassigns in 30s -> mark flapping.
rachel: agree. also suggest cooldown duration be eviction-type aware: preemptible 8s, hotspot 45s.
anya: also emit metric `fallback_amplification` so scaler can decide to create a temporary low-confidence scale intent.
deep: implementation plan: allocator labels shard state (healthy, suspect, flapping). fallback policy deprioritizes suspect/flapping shards. behind FF.
rachel: add SDK hint `prefer_stable_shard=true` for clients to opt-in.
anya: rollout: FF + canary sim for 48h. I'll write up a short RFC with thresholds and tests. ping @orch-bot when PR lands so CI runs the sim.
